chainA.claim: The v6 synthetic interval implementation repairs the v5 inverse-affine endpoint defect and reports the frozen finite-population stop decision correctly.

chainB.claim: A distinct freshness-obligation prototype can distinguish local-receipt freshness from cross-domain source-event age and can preserve a limited fixed-source-path information-sufficiency claim.

scope.separationRule: Chain B does not cure Chain A's synthetic finite-population failures, missing external registration evidence, calibration limitations, or deployment-generalization gap. Chain A does not validate the C++ obligation prototype.

chainA.bindingLimit: The hashes bind the current bytes and regenerated result, but all three artifacts are untracked in the current worktree and have no repository commit or external timestamp.

chainB.bindingLimit: The replay artifact binds its local replay script/test and fixed public-source commits, blobs, and line slices. The freshness certificate binds the replay bytes and C++ header but does not record hashes for its own JavaScript generator or test. The local audit artifacts are untracked and are not externally timestamped.

endpointChecks.formula: For each anchor-reference endpoint and each strictly-positive rate endpoint, evaluate anchorReference + senderDelta / rate and take the minimum and maximum.
endpointChecks.mathematicalAssessment: For a rectangular anchor/rate set and a fixed sender delta, the map is monotone in anchor and monotone in rate with direction determined by the delta sign. Four endpoint combinations therefore attain the real-arithmetic extrema when every admissible rate is strictly positive.

highMagnitudeSafeIntegerCounterexample.consequence: The endpoint formula is repaired, but the Number implementation is not a machine-rigorous outward-rounded enclosure over all finite safe-integer inputs.

truthUse.assessment: There is no direct test-truth leakage into the non-oracle method input. The wrong-rate control is nevertheless perfectly outcome-aligned through record order, so it is an adversarial witness rather than an unbiased ablation or natural-error experiment.

publicReplay.interpretation: This is a constructive information-sufficiency witness for the frozen visible operands, not evidence that either deployment actually uses different or unsynchronized clocks.

adapterSharing.autowareAdapter: BigInt subtraction, conversion to seconds as Number, strict greater-than comparison against a seconds parameter.
adapterSharing.carmaAdapter: BigInt subtraction and strict greater-than comparison against an integer millisecond duration.
adapterSharing.specialization: buildCaseClosure selects [0,2000000000] only when caseId is POS-01-AUTOWARE-VTL and [0,300000000] otherwise.
adapterSharing.renameCounterexample: Renaming the Autoware case while keeping visible timing operands fixed changed the bounded result from uncertain to timeout.
adapterSharing.assessment: The decision kernel is shared and generic, but the full two-adapter pilot contains repository/case-specific witness construction. The recorded claim must be narrowed accordingly.

mutationAssessment.assessment: The suite is useful branch-execution evidence for five constructed cases, but it is substantially self-referential and does not establish the broad claim that every malformed relation fails closed.

findings.title: The v5 first-order inverse-affine defect is repaired at the formula level
evidence: scripts/idea-pilots/clock-age-identifiability-v6.mjs:769-838 evaluates all anchor/rate endpoint combinations and rejects a nonpositive lower rate.
test/clock-age-identifiability-v6.test.mjs:298-361 covers both sender-delta signs and a nonpositive rate interval.
Independent interior sampling found no point outside the endpoint extrema, and exact-zero plus negative lower-rate cases returned invalid/uncertain.
findings.conclusion: The exact endpoint formula is correct for the declared rectangular real-arithmetic model with strictly positive rates. The stronger all-finite-Number conservative-enclosure claim remains blocked by lack of outward rounding and input-range enforcement.

findings.title: Exact event counts reproduce and v6 still stops
evidence: Independent grouping reproduced 219/252 every-covered clusters, one false-fresh cluster, one false-stale cluster, and 379/504 uncertain records.
The false-fresh report retains numerator 1, denominator 252, unrounded comparisonValue 1/252, and a separate display value.
Independent execution reproduced the four failed checks and stop-at-finite-population-methodology-audit.
findings.conclusion: The endpoint repair does not convert the synthetic method result into a continuation result. The finite-population failures and missing external registration evidence remain active.

findings.title: Non-oracle method input is truth-free, but the wrong-rate control is outcome-aligned
evidence: prepareMethodInput returns only record.observation, and changing record.truth did not change non-oracle predictions.
Synthetic calibration fitting uses calibrationTruth to obtain residual bounds.
All 252 fresh rate-stress records receive the positive mutation and all 252 stale records receive the negative mutation through deterministic record order.
findings.conclusion: The main test prediction path has no direct truth leakage. The wrong-rate experiment can support sensitivity and width/error tradeoff claims only; it cannot support natural-error, causal-contribution, or unbiased-ablation claims.

findings.title: Malformed validity bounds can bypass the fail-closed guard
evidence: scripts/idea-pilots/clock-age-identifiability-v6.mjs:851-855 checks only object presence and JavaScript comparisons.
An input with transform.validity={} passed those comparisons and returned status=identified, verdict=fresh.
The existing suite covers a missing whole validity object and an expired finite interval, not missing/nonfinite validity members.
findings.conclusion: The broad validity-check claim is false. This bug does not change the frozen v6 stop result because generated validity bounds are finite and populated, but it blocks use of this implementation as a general fail-closed gate.

findings.title: Endpoint results are not outward-rounded
evidence: The implementation uses Number arithmetic and Math.min/Math.max without next-down/next-up expansion.
Fixed endpoint tests have sub-1e-9 ms inward errors against exact rational arithmetic.
A finite safe-integer case underreached the real lower endpoint by 0.132660915 ms and the real upper endpoint by 0.142823567 ms.
findings.conclusion: The formula repair is valid, but strict machine-level endpoint conservatism is not established outside a bounded numeric domain with an explicit tolerance. This does not reverse the current stop.

findings.title: Current grid and event decisions are correct, but two stop checks are not encoded from exact primitives
evidence: The current bounded population independently contains all 252 unique grid cells with two records each.
completeFiniteGrid checks only total cluster count against 252 rather than unique cell identity and multiplicity.
boundedUncertainRecordRate compares a six-decimal rounded rate rather than integer counts; the current 379/504 result is far from a rounding ambiguity and still fails.
findings.conclusion: No current count or stop result changes, but future boundary cases should be decided from exact counts and explicit grid keys.

findings.title: A hash and input binding is internally consistent only
evidence: The pilot regenerated byte-for-byte and its recorded script, test, DGP, calibration, population, and audit-result hashes match.
The artifacts are untracked and have no git history.
externalTimestamp and immutableCommit remain null.
findings.conclusion: Current-byte reproducibility is passable; temporal ordering, immutable preregistration, and result-independent design freezing are not established.

findings.title: Well-formed JavaScript obligation behavior matches its narrow contract
evidence: Strict and inclusive exact-boundary verdicts are fresh and timeout respectively.
Intervals [50,51] under > and [49,50] under >= return uncertain.
Closed validity endpoints resolve; wrong domain, wrong relock, wholly negative age, and same-domain negative age fail closed.
A 101-digit BigInt age evaluates without overflow.
findings.conclusion: The JavaScript prototype can retain claims about these explicitly tested, structurally valid inputs. This is executable contract behavior, not production validation.

findings.title: Malformed relation shapes throw instead of returning uncertain
evidence: scripts/idea-pilots/clock-freshness-obligation.mjs:91-129 dereferences validity and offset members before a total structural validation.
Missing validity, empty validity, missing offset bounds, and non-integer offset values all threw in directed tests.
The recorded mutation suite does not contain these shape/type mutations.
findings.conclusion: The claim that malformed relation evidence always fails closed is blocked. Only the five recorded malformed-value branches are passable.

findings.title: The C++ implementation has unchecked int64 signed overflow
evidence: clock_obligation.hpp:94 subtracts receipt from now without a checked wider intermediate.
clock_obligation.hpp:156-165 adds source offsets and subtracts mapped timestamps without checked arithmetic.
UBSan aborted on INT64_MAX - (-1) and INT64_MAX + 1.
findings.conclusion: No general runtime-safety or fail-closed claim is passable for the C++ prototype until every arithmetic operation is checked. The recorded small examples remain reproducible.

findings.title: Compile rejection proves only the absence of selected wrapper operations
evidence: The recorded negative controls reject now - event and source-event substitution into since_local_receipt.
The Timestamp.nanoseconds fields are public.
A directed now.nanoseconds - event.nanoseconds cross-domain subtraction compiled and ran.
findings.conclusion: It is passable that the two selected wrapper expressions fail to compile. It is not passable that the type interface prevents bare cross-domain arithmetic or enforces obligation use.

findings.title: The mutation suite exercises branches but substantially self-certifies
evidence: buildMutationSuite constructs relations and calls the same evaluateFreshnessObligation implementation under audit.
runObligationPilot checks those generated results and then emits literal true check fields.
The test reruns the same builder/evaluator and does not use an independent oracle or implementation mutations.
findings.conclusion: The suite supports branch-execution evidence for its five cases, not completeness, semantic correctness for arbitrary malformed inputs, or mutation-test adequacy.

findings.title: The evaluator is generic but the full closure contains case-specific witness logic
evidence: The two public replay adapters are separate and preserve different unit conversions.
evaluateFreshnessObligation and buildMutationSuite do not branch on repository identity.
buildCaseClosure branches explicitly on POS-01-AUTOWARE-VTL to select the offset witness.
Renaming the case with unchanged timing operands changed the bounded verdict.
findings.conclusion: The claim may state that the decision kernel and mutation classes are shared. It may not state that the complete two-adapter closure is free of repository/case-specific decision-affecting logic.

findings.title: Bounded and receipt controls are deliberately truth-informed constructions
evidence: The v5 bounded control derives bounds from the two constructed hidden world offsets.
The v6 closure hardcodes bounds that straddle each selected source threshold.
The receipt control sets receipt time to now minus half the threshold.
The bare cross-domain case still receives no relation and returns uncertain.
findings.conclusion: There is no hidden truth fed into the bare unresolved decision. The positive controls are constructed witnesses and cannot estimate field calibration quality, utility, error rates, or deployment behavior.

findings.title: The v5 public replay is strongly bound, while the v6 freshness certificate omits two local source hashes
evidence: Both fixed public repositories, commits, clean worktrees, file hashes, line slices, extracted operands, thresholds, comparators, and branches reverified.
The v5 replay's recorded local script/test hashes match current bytes.
The v6 freshness script pins the entire replay JSON and records the C++ header hash.
The v6 freshness output does not record its own JavaScript script or test hashes.
findings.conclusion: The fixed-source-path replay and its claim boundary are reproducible. The freshness certificate should add self-contained local source/test provenance; none of these hashes establish deployment behavior or external registration.

findings.title: The obligation prototype does not convert the synthetic interval method into a usable deployed gate
evidence: Chain A still stops on three synthetic finite-population method checks plus missing external registration evidence.
Chain B relations and receipt timestamps are constructed witnesses, not calibrated field guarantees.
Chain B has malformed-input, C++ overflow, compile-enforcement, and adapter-specialization defects.
findings.conclusion: Retain the two chains as distinct evidence: A demonstrates a repaired formula but a stopped synthetic run; B demonstrates a limited obligation/interface concept and fixed-source information-sufficiency witness. Neither establishes real deployment validity.

passableClaims.claim: For the declared rectangular anchor/rate uncertainty model with strictly positive rates, v6 evaluates the correct four inverse-affine endpoint combinations and takes their extrema.
passableClaims.boundary: Formula-level real-arithmetic claim only; strict machine enclosure over arbitrary finite Number magnitudes requires outward rounding or a proven numeric domain.

passableClaims.claim: A rate interval whose lower endpoint is exactly zero or negative returns invalid and the interval method returns uncertain.
passableClaims.boundary: Verified for the JavaScript method path; this does not validate any external relation provider.

passableClaims.claim: The frozen v6 bounded population has 252 unique grid cells and 504 records, with exact observed counts of 219 every-covered clusters, one false-fresh cluster, one false-stale cluster, and 379 uncertain records.
passableClaims.boundary: Exact description of this generated finite population only; not a confidence bound, risk bound, or deployment estimate.

passableClaims.claim: The observed v6 action remains stop-at-finite-population-methodology-audit with four independently reproduced failed checks.
passableClaims.boundary: A method-audit action for this run, not a candidate score or statement about a real system.

passableClaims.claim: Non-oracle v6 methods receive observations and calibration only, not test truth.
passableClaims.boundary: The wrong-rate control remains outcome-aligned and synthetic calibration fitting uses calibration truth.

passableClaims.claim: The tested missing-whole-field, expired-validity, wrong-domain, nonpositive-rate, and relock-mismatch branches return uncertain.
passableClaims.boundary: Does not include structurally incomplete/nonfinite validity members, which can bypass the guard.

passableClaims.claim: The A pilot JSON is reproducible from the current script/test/input bytes and its recorded hashes match.
passableClaims.boundary: No immutable commit or external timestamp exists.

passableClaims.claim: At the two fixed public-source commits, the recorded visible subtraction operands, configured defaults, comparators, and immediate conditional branches match the verified blobs and line slices.
passableClaims.boundary: Source-level read-only replay only; upstream stacks were not built or executed end to end.

passableClaims.claim: For each of the two fixed visible operand tuples, two constructed monotone unit-rate mappings preserve the source-expression result while giving opposite reference-clock deadline truths.
passableClaims.boundary: An information-sufficiency counterexample; it does not assert that deployed clocks differ or are unsynchronized.

passableClaims.claim: For structurally valid inputs, the JavaScript obligation distinguishes local-receipt freshness from source-event age, preserves > versus >= boundary semantics, uses closed validity endpoints, checks domain and relock identity, and treats wholly negative age as uncertain.
passableClaims.boundary: Malformed relation shapes can throw; this is a prototype contract, not production validation.

passableClaims.claim: JavaScript obligation arithmetic uses BigInt and handled the directed 101-digit integer case without overflow.
passableClaims.boundary: Does not transfer to the C++ int64 implementation.

passableClaims.claim: The selected C++ wrapper positive cases compile and run, while direct wrapper-object cross-domain subtraction and source-event/local-receipt substitution fail to compile.
passableClaims.boundary: Public raw fields still permit cross-domain integer subtraction; runtime arithmetic is not overflow-safe.

passableClaims.claim: The same generic JavaScript decision kernel and the same five mutation classes execute for both replay cases.
passableClaims.boundary: The full closure fixture contains caseId-specific offset-bound selection.

passableClaims.claim: The v5 replay byte hash, fixed-source bindings, replay generator/test hashes, and v6 replay pin are internally consistent.
passableClaims.boundary: The freshness certificate omits its own generator/test hashes and local artifacts are untracked.

blockedClaims.claim: The v6 synthetic interval method may proceed or is a usable bounded-age gate.
The Number implementation is a strictly conservative identified-set enclosure for all finite inputs.
The wrong-rate experiment estimates natural error frequency or the causal contribution of rate metadata.
The A design was externally preregistered or immutably frozen before results.
A's finite-population counts establish any real-system risk, utility, safety effect, or deployment frequency.
Every malformed or missing relation fails closed without throwing.
The C++ obligation implementation is overflow-safe and fail-closed over its int64 input domain.
The C++ typed interface prevents bare cross-domain arithmetic or forces callers through an obligation.
The full two-adapter closure contains no repository/case-specific decision-affecting logic.
The mutation suite independently establishes semantic correctness or complete malformed-input coverage.
The constructed relation bounds are field-calibrated, the local-receipt redesign preserves source-event-age semantics, or either repair is ready for a production patch.
Either fixed public path is unsafe, reachable in a given deployment, supplied by unsynchronized clocks, or associated with a safety/performance effect.
Chain B repairs or supersedes Chain A's stop.

requiredFixes.fix: Validate that validity.fromSenderMs and validity.toSenderMs are finite numbers with from<=to; validate every arithmetic input and every computed endpoint as finite; return uncertain for missing, nonfinite, wrong-type, overflowed, or malformed members. Add empty-object, NaN, Infinity, and wrong-type tests.

Use outward rounding for mapped lower/upper endpoints, exact/fixed-point arithmetic, or a proven input-magnitude domain with a conservative numerical-error expansion. Add rational-oracle tests at both frozen and high safe-integer magnitudes.

Derive uncertain-rate decisions from integer numerator/denominator rather than a rounded rate, and verify the complete grid by unique declared cell keys and required per-cell multiplicity rather than cluster count alone.
Counterbalance or independently randomize wrong-rate signs across truth labels and report per-direction strata. Retain the current control only as an explicitly truth-aligned adversarial stress.

Resolve the independently reproduced finite-population failures and obtain immutable, externally timestamped registration evidence before a new unused run. Do not treat formula repair alone as a continuation basis.

Make relation validation total and exception-safe. Validate relation object shape, domain identifiers, validity object and ordered integer endpoints, relock representation, exactly two ordered integer offset bounds, comparator, and nonnegative threshold before dereference or BigInt conversion; return unresolved/uncertain for every invalid case.

Perform timestamp mapping and age arithmetic in checked __int128 or checked add/sub helpers, range-check before narrowing to int64, and return Uncertain/InvalidRelation on overflow. Add UBSan tests for every add/sub boundary.

Hide raw timestamp fields or expose only domain-safe operations if enforcement is intended. Add compile-negative cases for raw-field arithmetic, wrong-domain local receipt, wrong relation direction, and semantic-origin substitution. Otherwise narrow the claim to the absence of two selected wrapper overloads.

Remove the caseId branch from buildCaseClosure and supply relation evidence as explicit per-case input, or state that the closure fixtures are repository-specific while only the evaluator and mutation classes are shared.

Add table-driven malformed-shape/type cases with an independent expected-result oracle, and run implementation mutation testing that proves tests fail when each guard, comparator, negative-age clamp, or relock check is removed or inverted.

Record hashes for clock-freshness-obligation.mjs and clock-freshness-obligation.test.mjs in the freshness certificate, bind a canonical input manifest, and use an immutable commit when temporal provenance matters.

Define and independently validate a real clock-relation provider, validity/relock lifecycle, numeric range, malformed-input policy, integration boundary, and target trace/deployment population. Build and execute the relevant upstream paths and production-language integration; test passing alone is not deployment evidence.

chainA.summary: v6 repairs the v5 inverse-affine endpoint formula and preserves exact finite-population event counts, but independently reproduces the same four stop failures. Malformed validity can fail open and Number endpoints are not outward-rounded. These implementation defects narrow method claims and reinforce caution; neither defect converts the required stop into continuation.

chainB.retainedCore: Fixed-source visible-operand insufficiency, semantic separation of local receipt versus source-event age, and well-formed-input obligation behavior.
chainB.summary: The public replay and generic JavaScript decision kernel support a narrow constructive and executable claim. The malformed-relation throws, unchecked C++ int64 overflow, raw-field compile bypass, self-referential mutation evidence, and caseId-specific closure fixture block broader robustness, enforcement, and production claims.

verdict.finalStatement: The two evidence chains must remain separate. Chain A is a formula-repaired but still-stopped synthetic interval study. Chain B is a bounded obligation prototype and fixed-source information-sufficiency witness. No tested result establishes real clock conditions, production integration, safety effect, frequency, risk, or deployment effectiveness.
